question: A mobile phone worth ₹8,000 is sold at a loss of 10%. What is the selling price?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Loss % = 10% ⇒ Selling Price = Cost Price − (Loss % of Cost Price).

SP = 8000 − (10% of 8000).

10% of 8000 = 800 ⇒ SP = 8000 − 800 = 7200.

**∴ Answer = ₹7,200**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price = ₹8,000, Loss % = 10%

**Formula used:**

SP = CP − (Loss % × CP).

 
 Cost Price (₹8,000)
 
• 
 
 Selling Price (₹7,200)
 Loss ₹800

**Calculations:**

Loss = 10% of ₹8,000 = ₹800

⇒ SP = ₹8,000 − ₹800

⇒ SP = ₹7,200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,200 (Option 3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage Formula

Loss % = (Loss ÷ Cost Price) × 100

Selling Price with Loss

SP = CP − Loss, where Loss = (Loss % × CP).

Profit and Loss Relationship

Profit or Loss is always calculated based on the Cost Price.

Marked Price and Discounts

For discounts, SP = MP − Discount, where Discount = (Discount % × MP).
